originality.rationale: The exact nonreciprocal propagator, Gibbs stationary two-point function and corresponding Fourier integral are established in Weiderpass–Sharma–Sethi (2024) and the earlier directed Ising analysis of Godrèche (2011). The assessed new claim is the sharp post-exceptional-point stationary on-site *sign* boundary g_*=sinh(2 beta J), with infinitely many sign reversals above it, positivity at or asymptotically below it, and exact nonzero leading oscillation amplitude. The prior 2011 directed chain restricts nonnegative left/right influence p in [0,1], hence |eta|<=e; it cannot contain the oscillatory physical regime g>g_*>e. The 2024 primary full text contains exact kernels, wave and propagator regimes and low-energy two-point approximations, but no assertion or equivalent of this exact stationary sign classification. The result is a nontrivial analysis of known formulas; unindexed equivalent Bessel/asymmetric-chain work remains a risk.
residual_risks: A previously published analytic continuation of the 2011 formulas to effective drift |V|>1 or another Bessel-series sign theorem could imply the new boundary without using identical words.

value.rationale: The paper’s overdamped/underdamped boundary g=e characterizes the propagator. The additional g_*=sinh(2 beta J)>e separates stationary physical memory that stays eventually positive from memory with infinitely many direction-dependent sign reversals; the new phase is accessible only above the sharp temperature condition beta J<asinh(1)/2. This exact full-parameter sign classification is a motivated dynamical nonequilibrium observable, not a raw evaluation of a known transform or an arbitrary parameter slice.
